An authenticated caller denied an operation must receive 403 Forbidden.

What the Standard says

RFC 9110 defines 403 for a request understood but refused; rejected credentials instead belong to 401. read it here.

Why it matters

Enforcing this rule gives callers and maintainers one predictable contract and makes drift visible during the build. The analyser proves this specific source-level condition; it does not replace runtime acceptance or security testing.

Bad code example

// Violates RFC0007
catch (AuthorizationException) { return Challenge(); }

Good code example

// Follows RFC0007
catch (AuthorizationException) { return Forbid(); }
